assessments.reasoning: The exact-byte official log specifically marks underscore support between digits in numeric literals as a 3.46.0 addition. It establishes the timing and feature category and points to the expressions guide for details.
The matched official expressions guide explicitly dates the rule to 3.46.0 and describes one optional underscore between digits, ignored when interpreting the literal.

challenge.method: I compared the versioned release announcement with the exact expression guide. I tested multiple digit gaps to disambiguate whether the one-underscore limit applies per gap and tested two adjacent underscores. I compiled the project’s 3.46.0 amalgamation with loadable extensions disabled and exercised only an in-memory database. The amalgamation’s sqlite3.c SHA3-256 matched the 3.46.0 release log. The executable reported source ID 96c92aba00c8375bc32fafcdf12429c58bd8aabfcadab6683e35bbb9cdebf19e. https://www.sqlite.org/2024/sqlite-amalgamation-3460000.zip
challenge.results: The announcement and guide date the change to 3.46.0. The release runtime evaluated 1_2_3 to 123 and rejected 1__2 as an unrecognized token, matching the rule of a single optional underscore per adjacent digit pair.

limitations: The finding concerns numeric literals. The test covers decimal integer examples and the guide supplies the general documented language rule. String-to-number conversion and cross-engine portability are outside scope.
